The level pair matches the keys user_id, item_id. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Staleness: rerun at A-30 on the same labels. If the 1/k-weighted heat score keeps its gain over cooc_score with no decay, the gain comes from popularity and not from recent co-visitation.

critiques.text: Data at or after A: none; ev only. Batch dependence: none. cand restricts fi to candidate items and users restricts cu; tot and fc are global over ev. Twin: the rank permutation is ordered by hash(user_id), user_id and reads no table beyond the family. No leak. Not a leak issue: cohort_share has R2 0.993 to users_all and the twin is TWIN-BROKEN (rho 0.995).
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: cohort_lift in the users-with-recent-first-event stratum minus the long-tenure stratum. A zero difference refutes the cohort mechanism.

critiques.text: Item level and mentions neither cand nor users. All windows are [A-60, A) with sub-windows A-7 and A-30. The QUALIFY count is deterministic. Neighbour ROW_NUMBER has a full tie-break (co.k). The twin uses a hash(item_id), item_id ordered bucket permutation. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if nbr_mom30_tw gives the same gain as nbr_mom30, neighbour identity carries no signal beyond the popularity bucket.

critiques.text: Reads ev in [A-90, A) only. users restricts L and cand restricts HIT to pairs, keys only. Both ROW_NUMBERs have full tie-breaks (item_id; user_id). The RA filter on src items does not change any per-item value. The twin reassigns src_t by hash(user_id, src), src within the user. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if trig_tdecay_tw has the same gain as trig_tdecay, the trigger-time decay adds nothing.

critiques.text: User level, keys from users. ev only, all t < A. ORDER BY s DESC is unique because sd is grouped by (user_id, t). LEAD is deterministic. The twin picks a session by hash(user_id, s), s. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Key level: replace the user value by its decile mean across users. No loss of gain refutes a per-user session mechanism.

critiques.text: The user's last 3 steps are all < A. dn and di are per-step counts over all of ev; the t IN (us) and item IN cand clauses only filter, so per-step values do not depend on the batch. a30 is global. The twin shifts steps earlier by a hash offset of 1..28, so it stays < A and reads only ev. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if vday_share_tw (shifted steps) gives the same gain, same-step co-presence carries nothing beyond recent popularity.

critiques.text: Item level, no cand or users. Windows are [A-30, A) and [A-90, A), with first step taken over ev. ROW_NUMBER has a full tie-break (t, item_id). The twin is a deterministic hash(user_id, ...) Bernoulli draw. No leak. Not a leak issue: rho is undefined in the measurements, so a near-constant column is possible.
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: newcomer_share30 gain among new users (user_age <= 30) minus old users. A zero difference refutes the newcomer-affinity mechanism.

critiques.text: Item level, ev only, all t < A. LAG runs over DISTINCT (item_id, t), so the order is unique. The twin's global rank join is ordered by hash(user_id, item_id), user_id, item_id against t, user_id, item_id, a full order. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Staleness: the same query one anchor earlier. If silence_ratio keeps its gain beyond item_last, the gap normalisation adds nothing.

critiques.text: The pair window is [A-120, A). users only selects L(u) and cand only restricts j. pc per (i, j) does not depend on the batch. ROW_NUMBERs have full tie-breaks, and the twin's time permutation is ordered by hash(user_id, item_id), item_id. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if after_share_tw (time order destroyed) has the same gain, the directionality mechanism is refuted.

critiques.text: tl = the user's max t < A. The range(0, 8) offsets go backwards from tl, so all steps are < A. cand and users are key filters only. The twin draws a visit step by hash(user_id, t), t. No leak. Not a leak issue: the twin is TWIN-BROKEN on launch_vs_last_visit (rho 0.884).
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: pop_at_last_visit gain for users with recency > 30 minus users with recency <= 7. No difference means it is only users_7/users_30.

critiques.text: Item level, ev only. Windows are [A-150, A) and [A-120, A). LAG runs over distinct (user_id, t), so the order is unique. The twin uses a hash(user_id, item_id), item_id permutation. No leak. Not a leak issue: entry_share has R2 0.899 to users_90 and the twin is TWIN-BROKEN.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if followup_share_tw keeps the same gain, the follow-up mechanism is refuted.

critiques.text: Windows are [A-395, A-365) and [A-365, A-335), both strictly before A. users only selects L(u) and cand only restricts j. The transition count per (i, j) does not depend on the batch. ROW_NUMBER tie-break is item_id. The twin uses the same family with half-year-shifted windows. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if the half-year-lag twin (A-212/A-182) gives equal gain, yearly seasonality is refuted.

critiques.text: The user pace comes from the user's own steps < A. Item counts come from windows t >= A-k, all < A, with cand items only as a filter. quantile_cont is deterministic. The twin assigns pace by hash(user_id) % 6 and reads only ev, cand and users. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if pace_trend_tw (random pace) matches the gain, matching the window to the user's pace adds nothing.

critiques.text: e.t > lt.tl selects neighbour events after the user's last visit but still in ev, so t < A; there is no future data. Neighbour weights come from ev over all users and do not depend on the batch. QUALIFY has a full tie-break (ov.v). The twin uses a hash(user_id), user_id bucket permutation. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: gain for users with recency >= 14 minus recency <= 2. If equal, the 'since last visit' mechanism is refuted.

critiques.text: Session gap states come from all of ev in [A-425, A) and [A-60, A); ub uses max(t) < A. The cand item filter and users filter only restrict keys. LAG runs over distinct (user_id, s). The twin assigns the bucket by hash(user_id) % 10. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if state_lift_tw with random buckets has the same gain, the recency-state mechanism is refuted.

critiques.text: t0 = min(t) of ev is a global constant and does not depend on the batch. ft < A. ROW_NUMBER tie-break is item_id. The twin permutes ft inside count buckets by hash(item_id), item_id. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if launch_cohort_kern_tw gives equal gain, the launch-cohort affinity is refuted.

critiques.text: machine_red: probe_day_1 timeout after 20 s for both the card and the twin. The O self-join over all history before A-180 is unbounded. No leak in the SQL itself.
critiques.kill_test: Key level: restrict O to [A-365, A-180). If it still times out or loses all coverage, the card cannot run.

critiques.text: Item level, no cand or users. The backtest table fits growth from [A-30, A) on states at A-30, using only ev < A. Each current item uses its own state at A. The twin keys the age bucket by hash(item_id) % 10. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Staleness: one anchor earlier. If cohort_exp_growth gives no gain beyond users_30 (R2 0.902), the expected-growth mechanism is refuted.

critiques.text: The transition matrix comes from [A-180, A). The last basket is at max t < A for users. The cand item filter only restricts keys. QUALIFY tie-break is p.j. LEAD runs over distinct steps. The twin uses a hash(user_id, item_id), item_id time permutation. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if mc2_basket_tw matches the gain, the sequential transition order is refuted.

critiques.text: Item level, ev only, all t < A. f.n counts events up to A-1, which is inside the history. The twin's global permutation is ordered by hash(user_id, item_id), user_id, item_id. No leak. Not a leak issue: trendsetter_sum is TWIN-BROKEN (rho 0.990) with R2 0.923 to users_90.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if trendsetter_mean_tw gives the same gain, early-adopter identity is refuted.

critiques.text: Item level, ev only, all t < A. The twin permutation is hash-ordered with a full tie-break. No leak. Not a leak issue: launch_rate has R2 1.0 to users_all and the twin is TWIN-BROKEN, so it is a duplicate.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if launch_late_share_tw gives the same gain, the late-mass mechanism is refuted.

critiques.text: Item level, no cand or users. Newcomers have their first step >= A-30, all < A. The counts are global. The twin's user pick is ordered by hash(user_id), user_id. No leak. Not a leak issue: newc_lift has R2 1.0 to users_30 and newc_share has undefined rho.
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: gain among new users (user_age <= 30) minus old users. Zero refutes newcomer affinity.

critiques.text: Item level, ev only, avg(A - t) over t < A. The twin permutation is ordered by hash(item_id), item_id inside count buckets. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Staleness: one anchor earlier. No gain beyond global_rank (R2 0.913) refutes the mechanism.

critiques.text: User level, keys from users. L(u) comes from ev < A and the cooc statistics from [A-180, A). ROW_NUMBER tie-break is item_id. The twin uses a hash bucket item permutation. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if hist_cohesion_tw gives equal gain (rho 0.769 to the same neighbour), cohesion adds nothing.

critiques.text: Basket sizes come from [A-180, A) over all users. jb is per item with a cand-item filter only; ub is per user over history < A. The twin pairs items by hash(item_id), item_id in buckets. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: basket_gap gain for heavy-basket users minus single-item users. Zero refutes basket-size matching.

critiques.text: Item level, ev only. LAG runs over distinct (item_id, t). The twin permutation is ordered by hash(item_id), item_id. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Staleness: one anchor earlier. If dormancy_ratio adds nothing beyond item_last (R2 0.892), the mechanism is refuted.

critiques.text: Item level, no cand or users. Returning users are defined by a gap >= 60 before [A-30, A), all < A. The twin pick is ordered by hash(user_id), user_id. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: ret_lift gain for users with recency gap >= 60 minus active users. Zero refutes returner affinity.

critiques.text: Item level. Weekly buckets come from t >= A-91 and floor((A-1-t)/7) >= 0, so there is no step at or after A. regr is deterministic. The twin permutes weeks per item by hash(item_id, w), w. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if traffic_resid_wk0_tw matches the gain, the traffic-adjusted residual is refuted.

critiques.text: The ASOF join on last_t (< A) is deterministic. The cumulative window per item is ordered by unique s. The cand item filter and users filter only restrict keys. The twin picks a visit step by hash(user_id, s), s. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Difference of differences: missed_share gain for users with recency >= 30 minus recency <= 3. If equal, it is just pop_share_30.

critiques.text: Visits come from [A-180, A) and first_t is computed over ev with a cand item filter that does not change values. The twin pairs items by a hash(item_id), item_id bucket permutation. No leak. Not a leak issue: vis_since_launch has undefined rho and the twin is TWIN-BROKEN on it.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if vis_copresent_rate_tw matches the gain, same-step co-presence is refuted.

critiques.text: All cooc is in [A-60, A). L(u) comes from ev < A with a full tie-break, and the cand item filter only restricts keys. QUALIFY tie-break is k. 7.56 s is under the 20 s limit. The twin uses a hash bucket permutation of the hop item. No leak.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: twohop60_tw has nearly the same rho/R2 to users_30 (0.699/0.632). Equal gain refutes the two-hop mechanism.

critiques.text: Cooc comes from [A-180, A) and L(u) from ev < A with a full tie-break. cand and L are used as IN filters only, and co per (i, j) does not depend on the batch. The twin permutation is ordered by hash(item_id), item_id. No leak. Not a leak issue: co_support has R2 0.931 to cooc_score and the twin is TWIN-BROKEN.
critiques.kill_test: Twin as factor: if co_share_j_tw gives equal gain, raw co-support normalisation is refuted.
